theme: The earth’s final quake, the earth reporting everything done on it, and every person seeing even an atom’s weight of good or evil.
story: Reports differ on whether it came in Makkah or Madinah. Its short, powerful style fits the earliest Makkan period, when life after death and facing one’s full record were the core message.

Reportedly, when its last ayat came down, Abu Bakr stopped eating and asked, “Will we really see what we did of good and evil?” The Prophet ﷺ said the hardships they meet are the specks of evil, and the specks of good are stored for them.
Another report says it came about two men: one thought small charity worthless, the other thought small sins harmless. The Prophet ﷺ called its last two ayat “the unique, all-comprehensive ayah”.

sections.title: Earth quakes, casts out its dead, and testifies to what people did
sections.meaning: The earth shakes with its final quake and throws out its dead and its treasures. Stunned, man asks what is wrong with it. That Day it reports what was done on it, because its Lord commanded it. Then people leave in separate groups to be shown their deeds.
points: The final quake; the earth throws out its burdens
Man, stunned, asks: what is wrong with it?
It tells its news, because its Lord commanded it
People leave in scattered groups to be shown their deeds
sections.matters: The ground people walk on without a thought turns out to be a witness. Everything done on it is recorded, and on that Day it speaks. This sets up the rule of the next two ayat.
sections.story: No specific incident. Explaining ayah 4, the Prophet ﷺ said the earth will testify against every man and woman about what they did on it: “He did this, on such a day.”
explained: Idhā zulzilat al-arḍ: the earth is shaken from beneath with a quake fit for its size. It throws out its athqāl, its burdens: the dead and buried treasures. Gold and silver come out like pillars, and no one takes any. Man, used to firm, still ground, cries: mā lahā, what is wrong with it?

Then the earth speaks. It testifies about each person, what he did and when, because its Lord commanded it and it cannot disobey. People leave the place of judgement ashtātan, in separate groups, some to Paradise and some to the Fire, to be shown their deeds and what they earned.
teaches: The ground under your feet is recording what you do.
Nothing done in private stays hidden on that Day.
The wealth people sinned for will lie there untouched.
Even the earth obeys Allah’s command without delay.
sections.hook: Yawmaʾidhin (“that Day”) opens ayah 4 and ayah 6. The focus moves outward: al-arḍ, the earth (1–2), al-insān, man (3), an-nās, all people (6).

sections.title: Even a speck’s weight of good or evil will be seen
sections.meaning: Whoever does good the weight of a speck will see it, and whoever does evil the weight of a speck will see it. Nothing is too small to count, so no good deed is too small to do and no sin too small to fear.
points: A speck’s weight of good: he will see it
A speck’s weight of evil: he will see it
sections.matters: These two ayat are a complete rule for every deed, big or small. The Prophet ﷺ called them “the unique, all-comprehensive ayah”, and quoted them when asked about something nothing else had been revealed about.
sections.story: Reportedly revealed about two men. One thought a date or a crust of bread too small to give; the other shrugged off small sins like a lie, backbiting or a look, saying the Fire was only promised for major sins.
explained: Mithqāl dharrah: the weight of a speck, or of the smallest ant. If even that is shown and repaid, anything bigger certainly is. It is the strongest push to do good, however little, and the strongest warning against evil, however small.

The believer is shown his good and his bad; Allah forgives his sins and rewards his good. The disbeliever’s good is rejected in the Hereafter, though he may be repaid for it in this world. The evil meant is what was never repented of: sincere repentance is accepted.
teaches: Never look down on a good deed, even half a date or a cheerful face.
Small sins pile up like sticks gathered for a fire.
Repent now; unrepented small sins will still be shown.
Give the little you have; it may grow into much.
sections.hook: Ayat 7 and 8 are twins, identical except khayran (good) and sharran (evil). Both end in yarah, “he will see it”.

groups.text: The earth shakes violently, throws out its dead and treasures, and man asks what is happening to it.
The earth reports what was done on it, by Allah’s command, and people leave in groups to see their deeds.
Every speck of good and every speck of evil a person did will be seen.

1.explain: Zulzilat… zilzālahā: shaken with its own great quake, from beneath, at the Hour. Either the quake before the first Trumpet or the one when the dead rise; the context fits the second.

2.explain: Athqālahā: its burdens, the dead and buried treasures. Gold and silver pour out like pillars; the killer, the thief and the one who cut family ties see what they sinned for, and leave it.

3.explain: Mā lahā: what is wrong with it? Man is stunned that the once firm, still earth is shaking. One view: this is the denier of resurrection speaking.

4.explain: Tuḥaddithu akhbārahā: it tells its news. The Prophet ﷺ explained that it testifies against every man and woman about what they did on its surface, and when.

5.explain: Awḥā lahā: its Lord commanded it and gave it leave to speak. It does not disobey His command.

6.explain: Yaṣduru… ashtātan: people leave the place of judgement in separate groups, to the right toward Paradise or the left toward the Fire, to be shown their deeds and their reward.

7.explain: Mithqāl dharrah: the weight of a speck, or of the smallest ant. Even that much good will be seen and rewarded, so anything larger certainly will.
7.why: Reportedly revealed about two men, after 76:8 praised feeding others. One felt a date or crust too small to give; the other took small sins lightly, saying Allah only threatened the Fire for major sins.

8.explain: Even a speck of evil will be seen. This means sins not repented of, since sincere repentance is accepted. Beware of sins that seem small: they add up.
8.why: Reportedly it came down while Abu Bakr was eating. He stopped and asked if they would see all they did. The Prophet ﷺ said the troubles they met were the specks of evil, and the specks of good were stored for them.
